reading.rtitle: Two Boxes, One Shelf -- which cleaner is actually worth the money?
paras: Walk down the cleaning aisle of any American supermarket and you will find them side by side, at eye level: Riverbend Heavy-Duty and Meadow Gentle Wash. The front of each box promises the same three things, in the same big letters. A clean kitchen. A fresh home. A happy family. The front of the box is the least useful part of it. Everything that decides the question is printed on the back, in small type, under the word Ingredients. We bought both, used them for six weeks in three different homes, and read every line on both labels. This is what the small letters actually say, and which of the two is worth the extra money.

Riverbend is the stronger of the two, and it does not pretend otherwise. It is built for grease. The label says it breaks down the deep structure of cooking fat, which is a long way of saying that it removes what hot water alone leaves behind. One scoop cleaned an oven tray that had been waiting two weeks. It is also the cheaper of the two per load, especially in the value pack, which holds twice as much powder for six dollars more. The problem is the rest of the label. It is not fragrance-free, it is harder on your hands than anything else in the aisle, and the warning box is the longest we have read this year.

Meadow is the gentler product, and the quieter one. It is fragrance-free, it is gentle on skin and on color, and it dissolves completely in cold water, which the heavy-duty powder does not always do. On a coffee stain that had been sitting on a white shirt since the day before, it worked better than we expected, although it needed a second wash to finish the job. The scoop is smaller, the box is smaller, and the shelf life is shorter as well: nine months instead of two years, because there is less in it to keep it stable on the shelf. Per load, it is the more expensive of the two, by about eleven cents.

So which one is worth it? For most kitchens the answer is the gentle one, and the reason has very little to do with cleaning power. You use Riverbend twice a month and you use Meadow every single day, and the product you use every day is the one that has to be kind to your hands, your clothes and your nose. Keep a small box of the heavy-duty one under the sink for the worst jobs, and buy the gentle one in the normal size, not the value pack. With a shelf life of nine months, the biggest box in the aisle is the fastest way we know to throw money away.

listenings.text: Good afternoon, shoppers, and thank you for being with us today. A quick note from the front of the store. For the next three hours only, everything in aisle seven, and that is all cleaning products, laundry and dish, is twenty percent off at the register. You do not need a coupon. The discount comes off automatically when you check out. Two things worth knowing before you fill your cart. First, the twenty percent does not apply to the value pack of Riverbend Heavy-Duty, because that one is already on a separate promotion, so please do not carry the big box to the register expecting a second discount. Second, if you are buying more than you normally would, turn the box over and check the shelf life printed on the bottom, because a few of these are dated for March. The offer ends at six o'clock. Thanks for shopping with us, and enjoy the rest of your afternoon.

I want to tell you about the worst forty dollars I have ever spent. I had been in the country about a month. My English was fine in an office and completely useless in a supermarket, and I needed something to wash two wool sweaters. So I picked the box with the flowers on the front, because flowers mean gentle, right? Wrong. What I actually bought was a heavy-duty degreaser, the kind you use on a garage floor. The front said fresh and clean. The back said it breaks down grease and oil on contact, and that was the part I did not read. Those two sweaters came out of the machine three shades lighter and one size smaller. So now I have a rule, and it takes me ten seconds. I turn the box over, I find the ingredient list, and I look for two things: the words gentle on, and the word fragrance-free. If they are not there, it goes back on the shelf.

Thank you for choosing Meadow Gentle Wash. Please listen to the whole message before your first wash. Use one scoop for a normal load and two scoops for a heavy one. Do not guess. The scoop inside the box is the right size, and more powder does not mean a cleaner shirt. This powder dissolves in cold water, so you do not need a hot cycle. Thirty degrees is enough, and it is gentler on color. Do not mix this product with bleach, and do not mix it with any heavy-duty cleaner. Together they cancel each other out at best, and they damage the fabric at worst. If a stain is still there after the first wash, do not put the piece in the dryer. Heat sets a stain permanently. Soak it for thirty minutes in cold water with half a scoop, and then wash it a second time. Store the box closed and dry, and check the shelf life on the base.
